big: Last year, one fund topped the charts with a 45% return. Money poured in from every side. This year, it fell behind. The people who bought last, bought at the top.

lines: The best fund of last year looks like the safe pick. Why not buy it?
Because last year's result is not a promise. When everyone rushes in, prices are often already high. Ask what changed in the business, not in the price.

rows: Believing what happened lately will continue
Following the crowd because it feels safe
Money often arrives after returns have peaked
What changed in the business, and not in the price?
note: Past returns are not a guide to the future. Look at cost, risk, and fit with your goal.

title: Chasing winners
stops: Recency bias is expecting the recent past to repeat
The top fund of last year stays on top
A crowded theme is always the safest
caps: Last year's winner looks safe, but that is a trap.
Leaders change often, so last year's top is no promise.
A crowd buying a theme can feel reassuring.
Crowded themes can also be priced high.

q: Rohan wants to buy last year's best fund only because of its return. What is he showing?
why: Diversification spreads money, which is not what he is doing.
Rebalancing means returning to a target mix.
Careful research looks at more than a single past return.
He is assuming that the recent past will continue.

q: Everyone in Meena's office is buying one theme fund. She feels she must join. What is this?
why: Following the crowd because it feels safe is herding.
Allocation is a planned split among assets.
A stop-loss is an order to sell at a set price.

q: Why can heavy money flowing into a fund be a warning?
opts: It always means the fund will rise
It lowers every cost of the fund
why: Heavy flows do not guarantee future gains.
SEBI does not set the price of a fund at any time.
Money often arrives after good returns, near the peak.
Flows do not lower the costs of a fund at all.

q: Which question is better than 'what did it return last year?'
why: It focuses on the business, not on the past price move.
A logo says nothing about the business.
Others buying is only the crowd again.
Advert volume is not a reason to invest.

pts: Last year's winner is not a promise for next year.
Herding feels safe, but crowded themes can be priced high.
Ask what changed in the business, not in the price.
